messages:
oliver: heads-up — after last night's OFED roll (6.0.1) a bunch of training jobs in ap-south-1 are hitting massive NCCL transport slowdowns. seeing massive fallback to TCP for some ranks, overall throughput down ~3x. tagging @maya @dennis for infra/driver context

maya: confirmed. p95 inter-node bandwidth dropped from ~90Gbps -> ~28–35Gbps on the affected hosts. GPU util still high but synchronizations take way longer. started correlating to hosts with mlx5 firmware 16.28.2000 + kernel 5.15.87 + OFED 6.0.1 combo.

dennis: we pushed OFED 6.0.1 to euc3 and ap-south canaries yesterday morning. kernel module versions: mlx5_core 1.11.0, rdma-core 37.0.0. I see a spike in NCCL transport fallback logs: "NCCL_WARN : transport/ib : failed to create QP" on some ranks.

lia: quick debug from one affected node:
```
# ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
        transport:                      InfiniBand (0)
        fw_ver:                         16.28.2000
        node_guid:                      0x248a07fffe3b8c00
        max_qp:                          1048576
        port: 1:
                state:                  ACTIVE (4)
                phys_state:             LINK_UP (5)
                max_mtu:                4096 (4)
                active_mtu:             4096 (4)
                link_layer:             InfiniBand
```
but tx_err counters and "xmit_post_err" increasing over time. ib counters go weird when large concurrent grpc-ish small control messages happen during NCCL rendezvous.

jordan: workaround we've tested on one job: force NCCL to use TCP (NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0) — job completes but latency shoots up and costs increase ~4x. Not acceptable for production. Another quick workaround: downgrade OFED to previous canary (5.8.x) on a single rack and retest.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: rolling canary rollback to OFED 5.8.9 scheduled for rack-47 in ap-south-1 at 23:40 UTC.

dennis: discovered a vendor bug in their 16.28 firmware release notes mentioning "port blackhole under heavy QP create/teardown patterns" — likely our NCCL create burst. we'll validate with vendor but need an immediate mitigation plan.

maya: can we throttle QP churn? maybe bump NCCL_CONN_TIMEOUT or adjust GDR/KV cache prewarm to avoid QP storms. Also we should add an alert for NCCL fallback count and IB tx_err > 1000 within 10m.

oliver: action items: 1) open infra ticket with logs + ib counters + vendor fw note (assign to @dennis). 2) schedule targeted rollback for the most impacted racks (confirm with @jordan). 3) add short-term alert for NCCL fallback and IB tx_err (assign to @maya). 4) contact vendor SE for urgent investigation.

jordan: I'm creating the rollback runbook now. will include safe rollback checks: check ib counters are quiescent, ensure no heavy jobs, and a quick smoke with a small allreduce bench.

deploy-bot: rollback-runbook created: https://confluence.internal/infra/runbooks/ofed-rollback-rack-47 (ops only).

oliver: thanks. let's keep this thread for status updates. if vendor confirms firmware bug, we'll schedule wider hold on 16.28.2000 until patched. :eyes:
